Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin. The two Pakistan openers, Shan Masood and Abid Ali walk out to the middle. So do the Bangladesh players as they disperse to take their respective fielding positions. Ebadot Hossain will start the proceedings for Day 2.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the 1st Test between Pakistan and Bangladesh. On Day 1 Bangladesh folded up for 233 and Pakistan did not come out to bat due to bad light. Today they will start their innings and would look to occupy the crease for as long as possible along with taking a sizeable lead. Stay tuned for the action.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Abid Ali is shadow practicing his drives just outside the boundary. He will be looking to bed in on Saturday while Pakistan will hope to bat for 2 days at least and get a sizeable lead. Join us on Saturday, 8th February, 2020 at 10 am local (0500 GMT) for all the action from Day 2. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

The heavy roller is being rolled on and the umpires are checking the light meter. 5 overs to go (2 cut off for change of innings) but will we get those? The answer is NO. Nigel Llong and Chris Gaffaney are not happy with the light and have shut the shop. Off go the Bangladesh players (Pakistan batsmen did not arrive at all) and that will be STUMPS ON DAY 1.

Positives for Bangladesh? Many. With one common complaint - get in, but then, instead of bedding, throw your wickets away. Only Mohammad Mithun fought till the end and was consumed by a beautiful ball from Naseem. Though, he still believes that he was not out.

Shaheen Afridi was the pick of the bowlers, by far and large. He struck on the very third ball and then went on to take 3 more, as he ripped through the middle order. They were not necessarily good balls but the ones before those led to those dismissals. Mohammad Abbas was economical and accurate while Naseem Shah was just raw pace, without much direction or luck. Yasir Shah was not at his best at all while Haris Sohail was a surprise pick with 2 scalps.

A perfect bowling performance by Pakistan. They opted to bowl on a greenish track and picked up 2 wickets in the first 10 balls. They got a couple of fightbacks along the way but thanks to Bangladesh's heart-warming gesture of throwing their wickets away, the hosts get a chance to bat tonight (which, don't think they will be too happy about).

There it is then! 233 is what Bangladesh have managed to put on the board. After losing 2 inside 2 overs, they would happily take this total. This is Stumps time but because 7 overs are left in the day, play continues.

OUT! RUN OUT! Comical way to end the innings. Abu Jayed's bat got stuck in the ground and BANGLADESH ARE ALL OUT FOR 233. Full delivery on middle. Jayed flicks it to mid on and takes off for a single. Ebadot Hossain is not interested as he sends Jayed back. Abbas picks up the ball and then has a shy at the keeper's end. He hits and the Pakistan players are confident that Abu is out of his crease. The third umpire is called and the replays show that Jayed's bat got stuck in the ground just before he entered the crease. Out is the signal on the big screen and the players make their way off the field.
Are Bangladesh all out? There is an appeal for run out and it has been taken upstairs. The replays roll in and they show that Jayed's bat got stuck in the ground.
Good length ball down the leg side, Jayed looks to flick but gets hit on the pads.
Full and on off, pushed to mid off.
Another beauty! This one is angled away from the right-hander. Afridi pitches it short and on middle, it goes away after pitching. Jayed looks to force it to the off side but misses.
Brilliant yorker! It is on the pads, Jayed looks to flick but the ball hits the toe end of the bat and then his shoes. Lucky!
Good block in the end. Naseem targets the stumps this time as he bowls a full and straight one. Hossain brings his bat down in time to go through the over.
Angled down the leg side, Hossain looks to flick but misses.
Play and a miss again! Another length ball just around off, it shapes away as Ebadat looks to defend.
Beaten! Good length ball in the channel outside off, Hossain pokes at it to get beaten.
Ebadot Hossain is the last man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! It has taken the gloves and Naseem Shah gets his first wicket. After a lot of confusion, the umpire gives it out courtesy the third umpire. This is an excellent ball from Naseem Shah. Good length ball on middle, Mithun looks to defend but it seems to have gone off the bat to the keeper. The Pakistan players appeal but Nigel Llong tells them to wait and he asks the square leg umpire whether it is a clean catch. After a delay, Llong declares it not out. Azhar Ali, the Pakistan skipper is not happy and he opts for the review. The Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that it has gone off the gloves to the keeper. Excellent review from Pakistan. They are ecstatic and they have every right to be.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! Full on off, Mithun drives it through the cover region for a boundary.

OUT! TIMBER! The new ball does the trick and Afridi gets his fourth wicket. This is brilliant bowling from him. Full on middle, with movement into the batsman. Hossain looks to drive but he misses and the ball goes onto hit the stumps. Can he pick up a 5-fer?
Abu Jayed is in at no. 10.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.

FOUR BYES! Yorker down the leg side, with some movement into the batsman. It is bowled down the leg side, Hossain looks to flick but misses. The keeper dives to his left but fails to collect it cleanly. The ball rolls to the fine leg fence.
Fuller one down the leg side, Rubel attempts the flick but gets hit on the pads.
An appeal for LBW turned down. Length ball on the pads, Rubel looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. Pakistan players put in an appeal but the umpire is not interested.
Afridi starts with a length ball down the leg side, Rubel looks to flick but fails to get any bat on it.
Second new ball is available and Pakistan go for it straightaway. Shaheen Afridi will have a crack with it first up.
SIX! Hammered! Floated on off, Mithun thrashes it over the long off region for a boundary.

FOUR! FIFTY FOR MITHUN! 2nd in Tests for Mithun. Short delivery on middle, Mithun pulls it over the mid-wicket fielder for a boundary. It has been an excellent knock form him so far and now he will try to keep going. Can he get to his maiden Test ton?

Yasir Shah settles himself under the ball and takes a very good catch.

We are back for the final session of Day 1. The Pakistan players are in a huddle before making their way out to the middle. They are followed by Mohammad Mithun and Taijul Islam. It seems that it has gotten cooler with the umpires walking out wearing sweaters. Shaheen Afridi will start the proceedings with two slips and a gully in place.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

Another session left in the day! Pakistan would like to bundle the visitors as quickly as they can while Bangladesh would love to come out to bat in the first session of Day 2. Will we witness that or will we witness Pakistan bat in the coming session? Be back for the final session in a while.

Another excellent session for Pakistan. Just 77 runs in 30 overs and 3 big wickets. The session started with Abbas striking in the first over itself. Mahmudullah soon followed him and it looked like Pakistan might roll them over in this session itself. However, a 54-run stand between Liton Das and Mohammad Mithun saw the visitors bail themselves out from a tricky situation. However, as the stand was set to look threatening, Azhar Ali got Haris Sohail into the attack who broke the stand. Mohammad Mithun and Taijul Islam are still battling out in the middle and would look to add as many as they can to the board when they come out to bat.
Flatter one on the pads, Islam looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. No harm done. TEA ON DAY 1.

That beats everybody! Very full delivery outside off, Islam looks to dig it out. He misses and so does Rizwan. The batters pick up a couple of byes before the fielder chases it and cleans it up.
Full on off, Islam defends it back to the bowler.
Taijul Islam is the next batsman in.

OUT! LBW! What a masterful review from Pakistan. Nigel Llong has to reverse his decision once again. That never looked to be happening to the naked eye but the partnership-breaker has struck. A full ball down leg, Das goes for the sweep but fails to connect. He gets hit on the pads and the Pakistani players make an appeal. The umpire shows no interest. Rizwan, Pakistan skipper Azhar Ali and the bowler get together and after a quick chat, they take the decision upstairs. Time for the replay. Front foot is fine and there is no bat involvement which is confirmed by the Ultra Edge. Now, time for the Ball Tracker, pitched in line and hitting the leg pole, which means three reds it is. Das has to go.

Given not out, Pakistan take the decision upstairs. That looked to be going down the leg side. Let's see what the replays show. Well, that is pitching in line and it is hitting the stumps. Wow! We all thought that it pitched outside leg but that's not the case.
FOUR! Whacked! A half tracker on middle from Haris, Das goes on the back foot and dispatches it to the deep mid-wicket fence.

Full and just outside off, Mithun pushes it towards covers.
Fuller and around off, blocked.
In the channel outside off, it is left alone.
Length ball on off, pushed towards covers.
Fullish ball on middle, Mahmudullah flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Nicely done! Abbas bowls a shortish length ball outside off, Mahmudullah cuts it through backward point and bags a boundary.
Good bouncer! It is just outside off, Mithun drops his wrists and lets it go to the keeper.
Another good length ball around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Bouncer on middle, Mithun ducks under it.
Good length ball on off, Mithun pushes it towards point.
Good length ball outside off, Mithun pushes it towards covers.
Fuller and on middle, Mahmudullah nudges it towards deep square leg for a single.
Fuller and just around off, Mithun watchfully blocks it to go through the over.
Back of a length ball angled into the batter, Mithun initially thinks of leaving it alone but then decides to go after it. He tries to pull does not connect.
On off, Mithun defends it out.
Fullish and around off, pushed towards cover.
Another length ball on off, Mithun pushes it towards mid on.
Outside off on a length, Mithun shoulders arms.
Another bumper, this one is on middle. Mahmudullah easily ducks under it.
Back of a length ball outside off, Mahmudullah has no business with it.
Another ball on a length and outside off, Mahmudullah lets it go to the keeper.
Length ball on middle, Mahmudullah blocks it out.
Good running! Fuller and around off, Mahmudullah tucks it behind square leg and returns for a couple. 100 up for Pakistan with this.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Slightly shortish length just outside off, pushed towards covers.

Mithun is off the mark! A fuller ball on middle, Mithun looks to flick but the ball takes the inner half of the willow and goes towards mid on. They take the first run but the fielder there is bit lazy in getting to the ball. Seeing that, the batters scamper for the second.
Another good length ball around off, Mithun pushes it towards point.
Length ball on off, Mithun keeps it out.
Shortish and around off, Mithun taps it towards the off side off his back foot.
Fuller and around off, Mithun pushes it towards covers.
Afridi bowls this last ball of the over on a good length but again outside off. An easy leave for Mahmudullah.
Bowls this one on the line of stumps, Mahmudullah blocks it coming forward.
Another leave as Abbas goes even away from the off pole on a length.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Another ball on a length but wide enough for Mahmudullah to play, he makes a leave.
In the channel outside off, Mahmudullah lets it go to the keeper.
NO BALL! Afridi starts with a shortish length ball outside off, Mahmudullah lets it be. Afridi will have to bowl this again as he has overstepped.
Mohammad Mithun is the new man in. Shaheen Afridi will share the ball from the other end.

OUT! Caught! Abbas strikes in the first over after Lunch. This is a very poor shot from Nazmul. He did really well to defend out 5 balls but on this one he got tempted. Abbas bowls this length ball outside off, Hossain Shanto goes for the cut shot away from his body. All he manages is, an outside edge which goes straight to the keeper. Rizwan behind the wickets pouches it comfortably. The 33-run stand is broken and Pakistan start the session brightly.
Another solid defensive shot from Nazmul to this good length ball around off.
Good length ball around off, Nazmul keeps it out.
Landed on a length and on middle, Nazmul pushes it back to the bowler.
Another length ball outside off, this time Hossain gets on top of the ball and taps it towards cover where the fielder makes a diving stop.
Abbas starts with a length ball around off, Hossain Shanto pushes it towards covers calmly.

The players are back for the second session. Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mahmudullah, the two batters walk out to the middle. The Pakistani players are already out in the middle. Mohammad Abbas to start the proceedings in this session. 2 slips and a gully in place. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

We have an hour's break now. How can Pakistan pick wickets in the second session? By the looks of it, Azhar Ali's decision to field first seems to be more because of the pitch getting better to bat second, rather than wanting to exploit the greenery on the deck. Join us back at 1.30 pm local (0830 GMT).

29 overs of pace and 4 overs of spin in that opening session. Pakistan were on top for the first 30 minutes of a 150-minute session. But the next 120 have belonged to the visitors, in spite of losing a wicket. Afridi has been excellent, Abbas has been accurate while Naseem has given it his all, vying for raw pace but the line has been off the radar. No turn so far for Yasir.

Azhar Ali kept ringing in the bowling changes but Mominul and Shanto kept firm, not throwing their wickets away until Afridi removed the skipper, setting him beautifully. Since then, Mahmudullah has forged a decent stand with Najmul.

Azhar Ali's bowlers struck the perfect chord when given the opportunity to make the first use of a green deck. Debutant Saif and the experienced Tamim were nipped out early, in 10 balls and Bangladesh had their backs to the wall. But then, Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mominul Haque played perfect Test cricket after that. Started leaving a few balls, had some plays and misses, played a few shots, got some streaky boundaries but crucially, they did not get out.

Have to give it to Bangladesh. Yes, you choose to bowl and take three wickets in the first session - sure you would be happy. But to have a side reeling 2 down in the span of 10 balls and then to take only 1 more in the next 188, means that there is not much support for the bowlers.
Full and just outside off, Mahmudullah gets right behind that one to defend. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a single, just past short leg.
Around off, Shanto gets right behind this and defends.
This is driven towards mid off.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a couple.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Comes around the wicket, generates a straighter angle as he targets the stumps, Shanto works it through the leg side for a single. The stand moves to 30.
Fuller length now. Outside off, defended towards cover.
Back of a length outside off, punched straight to cover.
A length ball, around off, angling away, Shanto shoulders arms.
Full and outside off, Najmul blocks it out solidly towards cover.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full and around off, pushed straight to cover.

Excellent comeback from the seamer! A length ball, outside off, the former skipper is forced to play at it. Feels for it but the ball moves away a touch and beats him. Mahmudullah immediately swishes his bat through the air, visibly upset with his shot. That ball had everything in it - except a wicket.
FOUR! Well played. A full ball outside off, Mahmudullah gets a good stretch, is to the pitch of the ball and plays it through point.
Fuller in length, defended from the crease.
On a good length, around off, pushed towards point.
On a length outside off, allowed to go through again.
Landed outside off, on a length, watchfully let through.
A touch short, punched towards cover.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
On a good length outside off, let through once more.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Outside off, just a tad short, punched straight to cover.
Around middle, tucked through mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 40 now.
FOUR! Cracking shot. A short ball, outside off, Najmul gets on top of the bounce and cuts it through point!
A bouncer now, around middle, Shanto ducks. Close to a wide but not given.
A touch short, punched towards cover.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, driven towards cover.
Fuller, around off, Najmul, standing out of his crease, walks to the pitch of the ball and drives it straight to mid off.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Landed outside off, allowed to go through.
A length ball, outside off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Neatly done. On a length outside off, Mahmudullah waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it past gully towards third man!
Landed outside off, left alone.
A length ball outside off, Mahmudullah defends it watchfully towards cover.
Fuller in length, outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.

Is that a nick? 'AWAAZ TOH AAYI THI!' tells the kid to his keeper. No one from the slips is sure. What a jaffa to start your second spell. A length ball, outside off, Mahmudullah looks to defend but the ball pitches and then moves away, squaring the batsman up. There is a noise as the ball goes past (to my ears and Naseem's) but no one else hears anything. Awaiting the Ultra Edge, if shown.
Naseem Shah is back on. 5-0-20-0 so far.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
That is on a length, outside off, Shanto looks to defend but the ball moves away off the seam and beats the outside edge.
On a fuller length outside off, this is well blocked out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Mohammad Abbas returns. 6-4-5-1 so far.
Down the leg side, flicked wide of short leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Full and down the leg side, swept really fine, beating the fine leg fielder!
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
EDGED, FOUR! A touch short outside off, Mahmudullah looks to punch but the ball spins away and takes the outside edge. It flies wide of first slip, to the third man fence.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
A length ball, outside off, nips back in, Mahmudullah looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single.
Very full outside off, almost a yorker, Mahmudullah looks to push away from his body but gets a thick inside edge towards square leg.
Full and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Landed outside off, pushed straight to point.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a single.
Outside off, a touch short, pushed straight to point.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Around middle and leg, flicked towards short leg.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Mahmudullah walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! See, this is what happens if you keep Free Hit in one format after a no ball and not in another. Not justifying Mominul, but could that thought have come in his mind? Or did we just jinx him? Do not check 21.2 if you feel we did not jinx him. Full and outside off, Haque looks to drive but does not go too far forward. All he manages is a thick outside edge, which is snapped by the keeper Rizwan. Normally, the captain would have left it alone. But he went after this one. Could it just be, could it just be, could it just be - that he felt that this one was a Free Hit? Just asking... The 59-run stand is broken.
Outside off, left alone. A late call for a no ball is made by the umpire. Replays show that Afridi overstepped by a massive margin!
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to cover.
On a length outside off, punched straight to cover.

In the corridor of uncertainty, the captain could have flirted with this one, had a feel for it, but all this would have happened half an hour ago. Not now. Mominul is assured of where his off stump is and lets it go.
Full and outside off, good judgement from the skipper, shoulders arms on the angle.
Outside off, pushed to cover with a lunge.
FOUR! The runs are flowing now. Full and around leg, Najmul gets down and sweeps this very fine, beating the man at fine leg to his left.
This is on middle, Shanto drives it down the ground. But the bowler dives to his left and parries the ball to short mid-wicket. Good effort.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Tossed up, around middle, Najmul lunges and pushes it back to Yasir again.
Full and around middle, worked back to the bowler.
A leave outside off to end a healthy over for the visiting side.
Landed outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Another gorgeous shot! This is on a length again, the skipper just turns this in front of square on the leg side and gets the second boundary of the over!
Full and outside off, a touch wide, Haque looks to drive but misses.
FOUR! That is a lovely way to bring up the team's 50 and the 50-run stand! A length ball, outside off, Mominul just works it to the left of mid on and finds the fence!
Landed outside off, left alone.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover. An ordinary start by the leggie.
FOUR! Commanding shot. Full and down the leg side, Najmul gets down and sweeps this behind square leg!
Finally something in line of the stumps, watchfully defended.
Third ball on the trot on leg stump, worked straight to short leg.
Down the leg side again, Najmul tries to do what his skipper did on the last ball. The flick. But he misses.
Down the leg side, Mominul looks to flick but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. The ball lobs wide of short leg, towards square leg. A run taken.
Spin time! Yasir Shah has been called upon.

A length ball, outside off, Mominul looks to play this with an open bat-face. However, the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards the slip cordon. Lands just short of second slip who dives to his left but the ball lands short. Cannot stop it cleanly and concedes a run.
Pushes this straight to cover.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off this time.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and around off, well defended.

DRINKS BREAK. Well, if you are wondering, why has the break been taken after 80 minutes. This is a Friday, so we will be having an extended opening session. So, Lunch, which is normally taken at noon local, will be taken at 12.30 pm. Then, there will be an hour's gap for Lunch, due to the Friday Namaaz (prayers). Bangladesh have done well to recover after the early blows. Losing two wickets in the first 10 balls and not losing any for the next hour is a great achievement. Both batsmen have flirted with danger but have survived. Can they see off this extended session?
Landed outside off, moving away, shouldered arms to.
Outside off, on a length, punched straight to point.

FOUR! SWEET! Stunning shot to behold too. Excellent balance and perfect head position. Right on top of the ball, watching it till the last moment. Then extending his arms to play the shot. Picture perfect pose for the photographers. On a length, outside off, Najmul stands tall and punches it sweetly through the covers! He too, moves to 20, but has faced more balls than his skipper. The partnership is worth 40 now.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single. The skipper moves to 20 from 40 balls.
A length ball, around off, Mominul looks to defend but the cherry nips back in and takes the inside edge. Hits him on the pads.
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat towards cover.
Very full, outside off, squeezed straight to third slip now. Flirting with danger are these two.
Outside off, on a length, Mominul just opens the face of the bat and guides it towards gully. Shan Masood dives to his left and parries it towards Yasir Shah at backward point. A run taken.

Sloppy from Yasir. Najmul just plays this with an open bat-face, straight to Shah at backward point. He gets down, looks to collect the ball but takes it too lightly. The cherry hits his right palm and deflects behind. A single taken.
On a length, outside off, solidly defended.
Half volley outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.

FOUR! The Nataraja shot! A short ball, around middle, Mominul pulls it, ala Nataraja style, with his left leg grounded and right leg in the air, with the body swivelling across, to the mid-wicket fence!
Fuller now, testing the batsman's footwork, played straight to point.
A bouncer, on middle, Mominul has to take evasive action as the ball is coming straight at him. Just sways at the last moment, out of harm's way.
This is outside off, pushed straight to point.
Full on middle, worked through mid-wicket but straight to the fielder.
Around off, well defended.
Typical response from a fast bowler. A drive meets a bouncer next. Shanto ducks.
FOUR! SUBLIME! Shot of the morning so far. Overpitched outside off, Najmul leans and drives this through the covers for a boundary!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, well blocked out.
Down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket. Three runs taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A short ball, outside off, punched off the back foot.
A length ball, around off, coming in, the skipper rises with the bounce and tucks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
This is pushed straight to cover.
A length ball, outside off, left alone.

EDGY FOUR! Second one for Mominul. But this time he was at least not in two minds. A short ball, outside off, coming in with the angle, Haque is cramped for room but he still throws his bat at it. Gets a thick outside edge which flies over first slip to the third man fence.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another one in the corridor of uncertainty, played out watchfully.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and around off, driven towards mid off.
Around off, this is watchfully defended.

IN THE AIR... OVER GULLY! FOUR! The first boundary of the day and game comes in a fortuitous manner. A length ball, outside off, Mominul is not watching the ball and is looking to duck. But the ball suddenly comes in and he realizes that it is coming at his face. He now tries to just push the ball away meekly and it flies off the face of his bat, over a leaping gully to the third man fence.
Plenty of effort on this bowl, fired in from around the wicket, watchfully defended.
A length ball, just outside off, pushed towards point.
Good bounce generated by the youngster. On a length outside off, Mominul shoulders arms but the ball keeps on rising after pitching. Just about misses the bat.
A wide ball outside off, on a length, left alone.
Comes over the wicket for the left-hander and bowls it outside off, watchfully blocked out.
Full and just around off, this is perfectly kept out.
A straight ball, just a little bit of deviation away from the left-hander, Najmul is surprised and just about manages to defend it back to the bowler.
Wide outside off, let through.
Landed outside off, played straight to point.
The third slip has been removed for Abbas. Maybe because the batsman is playing with hard hands, feels Ramiz Raja on air.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Fuller, on middle, worked to the left of mid on for a single.
Landed outside off, let through.

Goes after this one now. Fractionally short of a good length, outside off, Mominul looks to guide it towards third man but gets a bottom edge which bounces and threatens to go over the keeper. But Rizwan leaps and stops it.
Another one let through to the keeper.
Full and outside off, angling away, left alone.
The first change of the morning. It is going to be Naseem Shah to bowl. Very fit, just like Shaheen Afridi.
Full and in line of the stumps, well defended.
Fuller now, well blocked out.
This one nips back in, from outside off, Najmul looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. Nearly drags it back on!
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Fuller, on middle, driven beautifully down the ground through mid on. Two runs taken.
A length ball, around off, tapped towards point.
Full and just outside off, the skipper shoulders arms.
This is a length ball now, outside off, calmly let through.
A bouncer now, from the 6-foot-5 lad, banged well over the batsman. Ducked under.
Another jaffa. A short ball, around middle, Mominul looks to defend but the ball straightens and beats the outside edge.

Excellent bowling but watchfully played. Full and fast, swinging in from outside off, Shanto watches it till the last moment and then uses his wrists to flick it to the left of mid on. Three runs taken by the time the fielder can get to the ball.
Play and a miss! Almost the third wicket. Full and outside off, in that inviting zone to drive, Najmul is sucked into it and almost nicks it behind.
On a length outside off, punched straight to cover.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
Back in the corridor of uncertainty, watchfully blocked out by MH.
Comes around the wicket and bowls it full again, outside off, again, Haque does not flirt with it.
The tempter, the sucker ball, full and outside off, inviting the drive but Mr. Captain resists.
LBW shout, the slip cordon is excited but that was pitched outside leg. Abbas did not really go up. He knew where that was pitched. On a length, Mominul missed his flick and was hit on the pads.
That is a fine ball. A yorker, around off, swinging in, but Shanto is upto it. Watches it till the last moment and digs it out.
Around off, well defended.
Works this through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed with soft hands towards cover for a single.
A bouncer now, around middle, Najmul ducks, with his bat hanging in the air, like a periscope. Just about avoids the embarrassment of getting an outside edge.
A length ball, outside off, left alone.

Good fielding by Yasir. Full and outside off, a touch wide, Shanto leans and drives this away from his body between gully and backward point. Yasir Shah gives it a chase from backward point and just when the ball is about to touch the ropes, he dives and stops it. Dangerous. But saves a run for his side. Three taken.
Landed around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full again, in line of the stumps, Najmul walks forward and defends.
Much fuller in length, around off, pushed towards the off side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Landed outside off, played straight to point.
A length ball, in line of the stumps, well defended.
Outside off, Shanto pushes this through the covers and gets across for a single. Is off the mark.
Full and around off, watchfully defended towards cover.
This one nips back in a long way, Najmul looks to tuck it to the leg side but misses and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Fuller and around off, watchfully kept out.
A short ball, around off, punched towards cover.
Another one let through to the keeper.
Landed outside off, let through.
In comes the captain. Mominul Haque walks in at number 4, replacing Tamim.

OUT! LBW! That always looked plumb and the decision is reversed. Just the start Pakistan wanted. Two wickets with the new ball. And we do not have even 2 overs completed. A length ball, in line of the stumps, Tamim, by virtue of habit, looks to flick but falls over in the process as he misses the shot. Normally, Abbas is very straight and you cannot miss the ball  when he is bowling. But Tamim does. He is hit right in front of the stumps and Abbas appeals, putting in an extended one too. But umpire Nigel Llong just asks him to calm down. There is a lot of chirp amongst the Pakistan fielders and Llong is telling them that there is not enough time left for the review counter to close. And just when it is about to get timed out, Azhar Ali signals for the 'T'. No inside edge as per Ultra Edge. The bat was nowhere close to the ball. Now, the pitching. In line of the leg stump and then straightening to hit the pads. Crashing into off stump. The decision is reversed and the Prince of Chittagong has to depart. What a blow to Bangladesh.

A huge LBW shout! Not given by umpire Nigel Llong and at the very last moment, Azhar signals for the review. No inside edge as per Ultra Edge. What will Ball Tracker say? Three reds and Tamim will have to go!
Beaten comprehensively. A length ball, around off, Iqbal walks into the shot, looks to flick but is nowhere near the pitch of the ball. Misses all ends up.
Landed around off, Tamim watches it till the last moment and shoulders arms.
A length ball, outside off, left alone.
Mohammad Abbas to share the new ball with Afridi.
Around middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket. An interesting opening over. Could have had two wickets.
Outside off, on a length, a play and a miss.

Ooohhh... interesting. A length ball, around middle, Najmul works it through the leg side and sets off, due to pure momentum. But the man at short leg reacts quickly and fires a throw at the striker's end. Misses. Najmul would have been gone!
Najmul Hossain Shanto walks in at number 3, replacing Saif.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! 3 balls. That is all it has taken for Pakistan to strike. Full and wide outside off, the debutant Saif cannot resist himself from having a feel for it. Goes for the drive and all he manages is a thick outside edge. It goes towards the packed slip cordon where Asad Shafiq gets across from second slip and takes it to his left. Nothing special about that delivery. Just the tentativeness in Hassan's mind to get his first Test runs. Poor lad. There will be criticism about his lack of feet movement and all but only he will be able to tell that he felt it was a loose ball and he did not want to let a scoring opportunity go by.
Landed outside off, on a length, Saif shoulders arms.
A length ball around middle,tucked through mid-wicket for a comfortable three. Some way to start off a Test inning...

A wonderful gesture from Azhar Ali. He walks across to Saif Hassan, who is opening alongside Tamim Iqbal and wishes him good luck. That is really, really good to see. Time for the game to begin. The man with a smiling face, Shaheen Afridi, to start off proceedings for the game. The Prince of Chittagong to face, with three slips in place. Here we go...

The players are slowly coming out from the dressing room. In fact a ceremony is taking place. SAIF HASSAN IS BEING HANDED HIS TEST CAP. Now, the opening batsmen come out to the middle, following the Pakistan players.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Shan Masood, Abid Ali, Azhar Ali(C), Babar Azam, Haris Sohail, Asad Shafiq, Mohammad Rizwan(WK), Yasir Shah, Mohammad Abbas, Naseem Shah and Shaheen Afridi.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tamim Iqbal, Saif Hassan, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Mominul Haque(C), Mohammad Mithun, Mahmudullah, Liton Das(WK), Taijul Islam, Rubel Hossain, Abu Jayed and Ebadot Hossain.

TOSS - The flip of the coin has gone Azhar Ali's way. PAKISTAN ELECT TO FIELD. Interesting choice. Don't really see teams choose to field in Asia, unless they expect the wicket to seam around for at least the first day.

Test cricket continues in Pakistan! Hmmm... a big thing in itself. So what if teams are still skeptical to play here. So what if boards are not sending their best playing XVs. We still have a contest. After a one-sided encounter in the T20I format, we now get ready for a bizarre Test series, where, the first Test begins today but the second is scheduled in the month of April, that is 2 months later! And in between the two Tests, there will be an ODI played too. Unthinkable and not quite understandable. Anyway, hello and a warm welcome to the first Test between Pakistan and Bangladesh in Rawalpindi.
